newsitem.title: UGANDA: Uganda-U.S. group wants to develop coffee industry.
newsitem.headline: Uganda-U.S. group wants to develop coffee industry.

text.p: A locally registered company formed by Ugandan and U.S. investors is negotiating to buy 51 per cent of the state-owned Uganda Coffee Marketing Board (CMB), officials of the government's privatisation unit said.
They said the company, Coffee (Uganda) Ltd., was the highest of four bidders, with an offer of $8 million.

Before liberalisation in 1991, the CMB had a monopoly of buying, processing and exporting Ugandan coffee. Since then private buyers have taken over most of the trade, posing stiff competition for the CMB.
Privatisation unit officials said the new investors were prepared to spend between $10 and $15 million to rehabilitate the CMB's coffee processing plant in Kampala, which is badly run down.
They also planned to develop a plant to process instant coffee.
Most of Uganda's coffee output is robusta, mainly used for making soluble coffee, but there is no industry to manufacture the product in Uganda.
Uganda expects to export 3.9 million 50 kg bags of coffee in the crop year to October 31, against 4.2 million in 1995/96.
